title: Query the LMFDB
when: finding number fields, elliptic curves, modular forms or other objects of the LMFDB with given invariants
checking a conjectured example, or the invariants of a small object, against the database
whenNot: proving anything: a record is data from a database, and only a Lean proof settles a statement
a collection or a column you are not sure of: the site refuses a name it does not have, and the answer is an error
a computation SageMath can do: compute_sage gives exact values without a network

collection.description: The collection of the LMFDB's API, such as nf_fields (number fields)

fields.description: The columns to match and their values, such as {"degree": 2, "disc_abs": 5}; empty for the first records of the collection

limit.description: At most this many records. 10 when not given

records.description: The records as the site gives them: the columns of the collection and their values

examples.title: the quadratic fields of discriminant 5
examples.note: The columns of a record are the collection's; this one is shortened.

implementations.description: The LMFDB's API (/api/<collection>/?<column>=<value>&_format=json) through the client of @seshat/models, one request at a time with a pause between two. The address and the pauses are settings of the host profile. Not run against the site: it is not reachable from the development environment, and the request is written from its documentation as remembered.

environment.site: www.lmfdb.org, or the address LMFDB_URL gives (a mirror)
